forms.details: A complaint was received via telephone by the Admin Department from the customer stating that the reports were not received within the agreed time limit. Due to this delay, the customer faced inconvenience and operational difficulties and was unable to submit the report to SEPA..
forms.root_cause: The delay in report delivery occurred due to miscommunication regarding the dispatch location. The reports were sent to the Noori Abad office, whereas the customer expected delivery at their Karachi head office. This discrepancy in delivery instructions was not clarified prior to dispatch. Consequently, the customers did not receive the reports within the agreed timeline, leading to delay in submission of reports in SEPA. The issue highlights a gap in verifying delivery details between the laboratory and the customer before dispatch.
forms.corrective: The issue was addressed immediately by sharing the reports in soft copy via email to ensure the customer received the information without further delay. Additionally, hard copies were dispatched to the customer’s Karachi head office through the M&P courier service to ensure proper delivery and closure of the communication gap.

forms.details: The "Reporting of Results" procedure (ETAL-LAB-P-708) does not specify which decision rule should be applied when the customer does not provide one, as required by Clause 7.8.6 of ISO/IEC 17025:2017. This omission could lead to inconsistent application of decision rules in test reports.
forms.root_cause: The root cause of this non-conformance is the laboratory's assumption that customers would always specify the decision rule for the Statement of Conformity. This assumption may stem from a lack of clear instructions in the procedure and insufficient communication with customers regarding decision-making rules. A detailed root cause analysis using the 5 Whys revealed gaps in training and procedure clarity.
forms.corrective: Revise Clause 6.3 of the "Reporting of Results" procedure (ETAL-LAB-P-708) to include a default decision rule (binary acceptance with zero-guard band) when the customer does not specify one. Update customer communication protocols to inform customers of the default decision rule when they request a Statement of Conformity. Conduct training for laboratory personnel on the revised procedure and the importance of applying the default decision rule consistently.
forms.file: Improvement_NC/Improvement NC/ETAL-QMS-710-FF-01 Non-Conformance Corrective Action Form - Revised.docx

whys: The laboratory assumes that customers will always specify the decision rule applicable to the Statement of Conformity in the test report
The lab did not anticipate the possibility of a customer omitting the decision rule, assuming that customers would always specify it as part of the process.
The lab's past experience with customers had always involved the provision of a decision rule, leading to the belief that it was a standard expectation for all customers.
rcas.conclusion: The NC was raised by CEO for the improvement of system , and RCA has been analyzed. The Lab manager will updated  the procedure to handle cases where a customer requests a Statement of Conformity without specifying a decision rule, adopting a default decision rule of binary acceptance with a zero-guard band.

forms.details: As per procedure ETAL-IMS-P-500, Section 6.5.1 under the communication section, Envi Tech AL commits to "encouraging employees to provide feedback on IMS processes and performance”; however, no formal feedback format or mechanism was found to be available or implemented. This indicates a gap between documented procedure and actual practice, affecting effective internal communication as required by the management system.
forms.root_cause: The IMS was implemented in 2024, and initial efforts focused mainly on employee training. Feedback was encouraged informally but not captured through a formal system. A structured format to document feedback was not developed at that stage. As a result, employee feedback on IMS processes was not properly recorded.
forms.corrective: The “Employee Feedback Form” (ETAL-IMS-500-FF-04) has been formally integrated into the system to ensure structured collection and documentation of employee feedback, aligning with the requirements of the communicating policy of ISO 9001 & ISO 14001.
forms.remarks: NC-01/IA-02/2025 is closed as the “Employee Feedback Form” (ETAL-IMS-500-FF-04) has been formally introduced into the system and implemented.

rcas.statement: No formal mechanism exists to record or collect employee feedback on the IMS, despite the requirement in Procedure 500, Section 6.5.1.
whys: Because there was no formal feedback mechanism or documented format in place.
Because at the time of IMS implementation, the focus was mainly on training of employees rather than establishing a structured feedback collection process.
Because management prioritized immediate awareness and competency building over setting up feedback systems, assuming informal feedback would be sufficient in the initial stage.
rcas.conclusion: During IMS implementation in 2024, the requirement for a structured employee feedback system was overlooked in the planning stage. Responsibility for developing a formal feedback mechanism was not assigned, leading to reliance on informal feedback and absence of documented employee input.

forms.details: As per procedure ETAL-IMS-P-800, Section 6.2 (Requirements for Products and Services), Envi Tech AL is expected to define and implement a process for determining, reviewing, and documenting customer and applicable regulatory requirements prior to service provision. However, the procedure lacks sufficient detail on how requirements are identified and reviewed, how changes are managed, and who is responsible for these activities. This gap indicates non-compliance with the documented process and fails to meet the requirements of ISO 9001:2015 – Clauses 8.2.2 and 8.2.3.
forms.root_cause: During the initial drafting of ETAL-IMS-P-800, limited focus was given to mapping procurement-specific processes for determining, reviewing, updating, and assigning responsibilities for customer and regulatory requirements. This gap resulted from prioritizing rapid ISO 9001 alignment over detailed process documentation.
forms.corrective: A new procedure titled ‘ETAL-IMS-P-802: Externally Provided Products and Services’ will be introduced and implemented to ensure compliance with ISO 9001:2015 Clause 8.2, addressing the requirements for determining, reviewing, and documenting customer and applicable statutory/regulatory requirements.
forms.remarks: Procedure ETAL-IMS-P-802 has been implemented to ensure compliance with ISO 9001:2015 Clause 8.2. NC-03/IA-02/2025 is resolved and closed.

forms.details:
Lab has not included residual risks in Risk Assessment Form (ETAL-QMS-805-FF-01), and acceptance criteria for residual risks has not been defined by the lab.
Lab needs to develop “Undertaking of impartiality” for Personnel, including any committee members, contractors, personnel of external bodies, or individuals acting on the lab’s behalf.
Lab needs to develop “Undertaking of confidentiality” for Personnel, including any committee members, contractors, personnel of external bodies, or individuals acting on the lab’s behalf.
forms.root_cause:
The laboratory established a risk management process focused on identification, mitigation, and periodic review of risks; however, the system did not include a structured step to evaluate and document residual risks after implementation of control measures, nor to define acceptance criteria. This gap occurred due to initial emphasis on risk control rather than complete risk evaluation, leading to incomplete implementation of the requirement to assess the effectiveness of actions as per Clause 8.5 of ISO/IEC 17025:2017.
Impartiality declarations were not formally extended to committee members, contractors, and external representatives, as the laboratory considered existing organizational controls such as supervision, hierarchy, and internal review processes to be sufficient to safeguard impartiality. This led to an assumption that formal impartiality undertakings were not necessary for all external or non-permanent personnel. As a result, the requirements of ISO/IEC 17025:2017 Clause 4.1 regarding the proactive identification, management, and documented commitment to impartiality for all relevant personnel were not fully interpreted or implemented, resulting in incomplete application of impartiality controls across all applicable roles.
Confidentiality undertakings were issued only to internal staff, contractors, and service providers, and not extended to committee members or external representatives. This was because the laboratory relied on an access control system outside the laboratory to restrict entry and assumed it was sufficient to protect information. As a result, there was incomplete alignment with Clause 4.2 of ISO/IEC 17025:2017, and formal confidentiality undertakings were not applied to all relevant roles.
forms.corrective:
The laboratory will revise the Risk Assessment Procedure (ETAL-QMS-805-P) and Risk Assessment Form (ETAL-QMS-805-FF-01) to incorporate a structured section for evaluating risks after implementation of control measures, along with clearly defined acceptance criteria. The procedure will be updated to ensure systematic evaluation of the effectiveness of risk controls in accordance with Clause 8.5 of ISO/IEC 17025:2017, and all existing risk assessments will be reviewed and updated accordingly.
The laboratory will revise the format of the Impartiality Undertaking (ETAL-QMS-401-FF-01) into a single standardized form applicable to all categories, including personnel, committee members, contractors, external bodies, and visitors. The updated form will be made mandatory for all relevant individuals prior to granting access to laboratory areas, records, or information. The Impartiality Procedure (ETAL-QMS-P-401) will be updated accordingly to reflect this change and ensure consistent implementation.
The laboratory will revise the format of the Confidentiality Undertaking (ETAL-QMS-402-FF-01) into a single standardized form applicable to all categories, including personnel, committee members, contractors, external bodies, and visitors. The updated form will be made mandatory for all relevant individuals prior to granting access to laboratory areas, records, or information. The Confidentiality Procedure (ETAL-QMS-P-402) will be updated accordingly to reflect this change and ensure consistent implementation.

the laboratory initially focused on risk management and mitigation rather than complete risk evaluation.

Because ISO/IEC 17025:2017 Clause 8.5 requires evaluation of effectiveness of actions but does not explicitly define the need for documenting residual risk or establishing acceptance criteria
rcas.conclusion: The laboratory’s risk management process focuses on identifying and controlling risks but does not include evaluation and documentation of residual risks after controls or defined acceptance criteria. rcas.statement: b) Lab needs to develop “Undertaking of impartiality” for Personnel, including any committee members, contractors, personnel of external bodies, or individuals acting on the lab’s behalf.
whys: The laboratory only required impartiality declarations from internal staff and did not extend the requirement to external or non-permanent personnel.
Because the laboratory assumed that existing organizational controls (supervision, reporting structure, and management oversight) were sufficient to ensure impartiality.
Because the impartiality risk assessment and ISO/IEC 17025 Clause 4.1 requirements were not fully reviewed during the development and implementation of the management system.
Because There was insufficient understanding and detailed gap analysis of impartiality requirements for all personnel categories, including external parties acting on behalf of the laboratory.
rcas.conclusion: Insufficient gap analysis and incomplete interpretation of ISO/IEC 17025:2017 Clause 4.1 during management system implementation resulted in the absence of a defined process requiring impartiality undertakings for all relevant personnel, including committee members, contractors, and external representatives.

rcas.statement: c) Lab needs to develop “Undertaking of confidentiality” for Personnel, including any committee members, contractors, personnel of external bodies, or individuals acting on the lab’s behalf.
whys: confidentiality undertakings have been issued only to personnel, contractors, and calibration/service providers, and not extended to committee members or other representatives acting on behalf of the laboratory.
Because the existing confidentiality control system was primarily designed for individuals directly involved in operational and technical laboratory activities.
Because committee members and similar representatives were not included in the defined scope of individuals requiring formal legally enforceable confidentiality commitments.
Because no unauthorized person is allowed to enter the laboratory premises.
Because it was assumed that physical and system-based access restrictions were sufficient to ensure confidentiality of laboratory information.
rcas.conclusion: Confidentiality undertakings were limited to internal staff, contractors, and service providers, and were not extended to committee members or external representatives. This was due to reliance on external access control measures, resulting in incomplete compliance with ISO/IEC 17025 Clause 4.2.

forms.details: The Lab needs to define and document the facilities like, equipment, fitting/fixtures, electric supply, gas supply, water supply, storage of Lab equipment /test items, as and when required for carrying out testing activities.
forms.root_cause: The laboratory did not properly define and documented all required facilities in the Facilities and Environmental Conditions procedure. This occurred because items such as equipment were already addressed in the Equipment Master List (Clause 604), so they were not redefined in the Facilities & Environmental Condition Procedure. As a result, supporting infrastructure such as electricity supply, gas supply, DI water system and fittings & fixtures were not clearly included or documented as part of facility requirements. This led to incomplete coverage of facility-related requirements in alignment with ISO/IEC 17025:2017.
forms.corrective: The laboratory will revise the Procedure of “Facilities and Environmental Conditions (ETAL-LAB-P-603) to include and clearly document all facilities available in the laboratory, including electricity supply, gas supply, DI water system, equipment, storage areas, and fittings & fixtures. This revision will ensure that all facility-related requirements are comprehensively covered in a single-controlled document. The updated procedure will be implemented and communicated to relevant personnel to ensure consistent application in accordance with ISO/IEC 17025:2017.

forms.details: Equipment ID is not mentioned in log sheet and correction factor of hygrometer is also not incorporated in log sheet neither in control chart.
forms.root_cause: The nonconformity occurred because the laboratory recorded observed values without applying the hygrometer correction factor and did not include equipment identification in the log sheets. This assumed that values within specified environmental limits were acceptable and that equipment ID in control charts was sufficient for traceability. The impact of calibration correction on actual environmental conditions was not fully considered during routine monitoring. As a result, accuracy of recorded data and complete traceability were not adequately ensured due to limited awareness.
forms.corrective: The “ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITION LOG (LAB) -(ETAL-LAB-603-FF-01A)” format shall be revised to include dedicated fields for recording both the observed value and the value after application of the correction factor. The correction factor shall be applied as per the calibration certificate of the hygrometer or weather station. All corrected values shall be utilized for plotting in control charts to ensure accurate trend analysis. Furthermore, the log sheet shall be updated to include a mandatory provision for recording the instrument identification to ensure complete traceability.

rcas.statement: Equipment ID is not mentioned in log sheet and correction factor of hygrometer is also not incorporated in log sheet neither in control chart.
whys: Because the laboratory recorded observed values directly and did not include equipment identification in the log sheets.
Because the laboratory assumed that the measured humidity values were within acceptable environmental limits and that mentioning equipment ID in control charts was sufficient.
Because attention was focused on maintaining readings within set limits rather than ensuring the accuracy of recorded values.
Because of insufficient awareness regarding the importance of using corrected values and maintaining complete traceability in environmental monitoring records.'
rcas.conclusion: The nonconformity occurred due to an assumption that observed readings within acceptable limits were sufficient, leading to omission of correction factors.This resulted from insufficient focus on data accuracy and traceability during routine environmental monitoring.

forms.details: The control chart of intermediates check of balance is with the same data point of intermediate checks used to calculate standard deviation and the independent monthly data are not drawn on control chart.
forms.root_cause: The nonconformity occurred because the same intermediate check data used for statistical calculations (standard deviation) was also used for control charting, instead of separately plotting independent monthly check results. This happened due to the assumption that intermediate check data alone was sufficient to represent instrument performance over time. As a result, routine monthly verification data were not integrated into the control chart, leading to incomplete representation of long-term instrument stability and monitoring trends.
forms.corrective: The laboratory will revise its balance monitoring practice to ensure that independent monthly verification data recorded in ANALYTICAL BALANCE IN-HOUSE CALIBRATION CHECK LOG (ETAL-LAB-FF-604-01) are incorporated into the control chart format ETAL-LAB-604-FF-11A, along with the baseline established from intermediate check results. All relevant historical monthly check data will be reviewed, compiled, and plotted to develop a complete and representative control chart.

rcas.statement: The control chart of intermediate check of balance is with the same data point of intermediate checks used to calculate standard deviation and the independent monthly data are not drawn on control chart.
whys: Because the same data set used for calculating standard deviation was also used for plotting the control chart.

Because it was assumed that intermediate check results alone were sufficient to represent balance performance. Although monthly balance checks are recorded, the data were not transferred or plotted on the control chart.
Because there was insufficient emphasis on using separate datasets to ensure complete and representative monitoring of instrument performance over time.
rcas.conclusion: The nonconformity occurred due to the assumption that intermediate check data alone was sufficient to represent balance performance, resulting in exclusion of monthly check results from the control chart despite their availability in records.
rcas.other: The control chart for the balance is incomplete as it excludes monthly check data and relies only on intermediate check results used for statistical calculations.

forms.details: Sample volume selection is not verified to get 2.5 mg to 200 mg residue for analysis of total dissolved solids.
forms.root_cause: The nonconformity occurred because the test method does not provide guidance for pre-adjustment or verification of sample volume prior to analysis to ensure the residue falls within 2.5 mg to 200 mg. As a result, the laboratory followed the method as written and selected sample volumes without prior calculation or verification. When results fell outside the acceptable range, the sample volume was adjusted and the test was repeated. This led to inconsistent pre-analysis control of sample volume selection and reliance on post-testing correction instead of preventive verification.
forms.corrective: The laboratory will introduce a pre-analysis verification step for sample volume selection to ensure the expected result falls within the required measurement range before testing. A calculation/check step will be incorporated into the "Lab Instruction for total dissolve solids " (ETAL-LAB-702-FF-03 (TDS)" to confirm appropriate sample volume prior to analysis, and analysts will be trained to apply this preventive control to avoid post-analysis adjustments and repeated testing.
forms.file: NC-RCA_Record-Internal_Audit-2026/NC-CA Record-Internal Audit-2026/NC-CA Forms/ETAL-QMS-710-FF-01 Non-Conformance-Corrective Action Form NC-05.docx

rcas.statement: Sample volume selection is not verified to get 2.5 mg to 200 mg residue for analysis of total dissolved solids.
whys: Because the laboratory did not perform any pre-calculation or confirmation to ensure the residue falls within 2.5–200 mg.

Because the standard test method (APHA) does not specify sample volume adjustment or verification before analysis that's why laboratory strictly followed the method steps as written without adding an additional control step.
Because the practice was to proceed with analysis first and adjust the sample volume only if results were out of range.
Because there was reliance on trial-and-error retesting to achieve acceptable residue values.
Because there was insufficient implementation of a preventive approach to ensure sample volume selection meets required residue limits before testing.
rcas.conclusion: The nonconformity occurred due to the absence of a preventive verification step for sample volume selection prior to analysis, as the laboratory followed the method without additional controls and relied on post-analysis adjustment through retesting to achieve acceptable results.

forms.details: Lab has not addressed this clause of standard in its QMS documents properly.
forms.root_cause: The laboratory has not established a dedicated procedure to address data and information management requirements because the QMS was primarily designed around document control (Procedure ETAL-QMS-P-803), with emphasis on version control and distribution of controlled documents rather than full implementation of Clause 7.11 of ISO/IEC 17025:2017. As a result, requirements related to software use, data control, validation, and documentation of verification activities were not formally integrated into the management system.
forms.corrective: The laboratory will develop a new procedure for “Control Data & Information Management System ETAL-QMS-P-711” in line with Clause 7.11 of ISO/IEC 17025:2017. This procedure will define who can access data, how software/LIMS is validated and how data is protected through passwords and backups. It will also cover control of external systems, and reference data for staff, and proper checking of calculations and data transfers with documented evidence.
forms.file: NC-RCA_Record-Internal_Audit-2026/NC-CA Record-Internal Audit-2026/NC-CA Forms/ETAL-QMS-710-FF-01 Non-Conformance-Corrective Action Form NC-07.docx

rcas.statement: Lab has not addressed this clause of standard in its QMS documents properly.
whys: Because there is no dedicated procedure for control of data and information management.
Because Procedure ETAL-QMS-P-803 was developed only for document control, version control, distribution, and availability of documents.
Because the focus of the QMS was placed on document control rather than full data and information management requirements.
Because the laboratory information system is still under development and only partially implemented (sample registration, reporting, raw data sheets).
Because software-based calculations were being checked manually before use, but these verification activities were not formally documented in the QMS.
Because Clause 7.11 requirements of ISO/IEC 17025:2017 were not fully translated into a dedicated documented procedure covering data control, software validation, and information security.
rcas.conclusion: The laboratory has not established a dedicated procedure for data and information management, as the QMS is mainly focused on document control and version management. This has resulted in incomplete implementation of ISO/IEC 17025:2017 Clause 7.11, particularly regarding software control, data validation, and verification activities.

forms.details:
a) Lab needs to communicate and implement objectives at all level of the lab as per requirement of clause 8.2.1 of  Standard ISO/IEC 17025:2017.
b) Lab has not established the responsibility of preparation and reviewing of documents
c) Lab has not described the style of 1st page of Level I, Level II, Level III and Level IV documents as their style are different  from each other.
forms.root_cause:
a) The laboratory has not ensured effective communication and implementation of objectives at all levels. Although all relevant staff attend the Management Review Meetings where quality objectives are discussed and responsibilities are assigned, the objectives are not formally acknowledged or signed by all staff after the meeting. This indicates that there is no formal mechanism in place to obtain documented confirmation of understanding and acceptance of assigned objectives, resulting in weak evidence of communication and implementation.
b) The root cause is that the laboratory was already implementing document preparation, review, and approval in routine practice; however, these responsibilities were not explicitly described in the document control procedure. This gap occurred because the system was initially developed with a strong focus on operational implementation and compliance in practice, while less emphasis was placed on ensuring that all existing activities were fully and clearly documented. As a result, the actual workflow was not completely reflected in the procedure, leading to incomplete formal documentation of responsibilities.
c) The root cause of the nonconformity is that, although documents within each category (policies, procedures, and forms/formats) follow consistent internal formats, the document control procedure does not establish a standardized first-page format across all document levels (Level I–IV). This occurred because, during the development of the procedure, emphasis was placed on defining document types and control requirements, while detailed formatting specifications for uniformity across all levels were not included.
forms.corrective:
a) The laboratory will revise and update the format of Quality Objectives (ETAL-QMS-802-FF-02) to ensure clear definition, assignment, and documentation of responsibilities. The updated format will include a provision for formal acknowledgment (e.g., signatures) by all relevant staff to confirm communication and understanding. This will ensure that quality objectives are effectively communicated, implemented, and monitored at all levels of the laboratory in compliance with Clause 8.2.1 of ISO/IEC 17025:2017.
b) The laboratory will revise the “Procedure for Control of Management System Documents” (ETAL-QMS-P-803) to clearly define the responsibilities for document preparation, review, and approval, ensuring alignment between actual practices and documented requirements.
c) The procedure for “Procedure for Control of Management System Documents” (ETAL-QMS-P-803) will be revised and updated to establish a standardized formatting style for all document levels (Level I–IV). This revision will clearly define the required first-page structure, layout, and content requirements to ensure uniformity across all controlled documents.
forms.file: NC-RCA_Record-Internal_Audit-2026/NC-CA Record-Internal Audit-2026/NC-CA Forms/ETAL-QMS-710-FF-01 Non-Conformance-Corrective Action Form NC-08.docx

rcas.statement: a)	Lab needs to communicate and implement objectives at all level of the lab as per requirement of clause 8.2.1 of Standard ISO/IEC 17025:2017.
whys: Because quality objectives were discussed and assigned duties during Management Review Meetings (MRM).
Because after assignment in MRM, the responsibilities for achieving these objectives were not formally documented and distributed at all levels of the laboratory.

Because the laboratory relies on MRM for setting and assigning objectives, but does not have a formal documented mechanism to communicate and record responsibilities for objective achievement across all levels, as expected under Clause 8.2.1 .
rcas.conclusion: The Quality Objectives format (ETAL-QMS-802-FF-02) did not include a provision for documented staff acknowledgment, which led to a lack of formal evidence confirming communication and implementation at all levels.

rcas.statement: b)	Lab has not established the responsibility of preparation and reviewing of documents.
whys: Because the laboratory was already following the process of document preparation, review, and approval in practice, but this was not clearly documented in the procedure.
Because more focus was given to implementing the process in day-to-day work rather than fully updating and detailing it in the documented procedure.
Because existing practices were assumed to be sufficient without ensuring complete alignment between actual workflow and documented requirements.
rcas.conclusion: The document preparation, review, and approval were being practiced in the laboratory but were not clearly defined in the “Control of management system documents” ETAL-QMS-P-803 . This occurred because the system focused more on practical implementation than on fully documenting all responsibilities in the procedure.

rcas.statement: c)	Lab has not described the style of 1st page of Level I, Level II, Level III and Level IV documents as their style are different from each other.
whys: Because the first-page style of Level I, II, III, and IV documents is not consistently defined across all document levels.
Because the document control procedure ETAL-QMS-P-803 does not specify a standardized first-page format applicable to all document levels.
Because the procedure only defines document types and hierarchy (policies, procedures, forms/formats), not their detailed formatting requirements.
-Because while developing the procedure, focus was placed on document control, approval, and identification rather than format standardization.
rcas.conclusion: The procedure for control of management system documentation does not define a standardized first-page format for QMS documents because its focus was limited to document types and control requirements rather than formatting specifications.

forms.details:
The Lab has developed the Procedure for Technical Record (ETAL-LAB-P-705, Issue No. 01, Rev.No.00) and procedure “Control of Management System Documents ETAL-QMS-P-803, Issue No. 01, Rev No. 00” to manage and control the Technical & Quality Records. Lab needs to revise these SOPs or develop another SOP for this clause of standard as these SOPs do not cover all the requirements of this clause of standard.
Lab has described the retention period for records as three years: lab needs to rectify its statement about the retention period as the retention period also depends on legal obligations.
forms.root_cause:
a) The root cause of the nonconformity is that the existing procedures Technical Record (ETAL-LAB-P-705, & Control of Management System Documents ETAL-QMS-P-803 did not comprehensively address the requirements of ISO/IEC 17025:2017 Clause 8.4 for control of records. Key elements such as retention, storage, backup, access control, archiving, and disposal were not fully defined within the QMS framework and were mainly covered under the technical records procedure only. In addition, record control requirements were distributed across the procedure of Control of management system Procedure without proper integration. This resulted in an incomplete and fragmented record management system that does not fully ensure compliance with Clause 8.4 requirements.
b) The root cause of the nonconformity is that the retention period was initially defined as a general requirement during the early development of the QMS. At that stage, it was set as a simple standard value without considering that retention may vary based on legal, regulatory, or contractual obligations. This approach was meant for general application and not reviewed in detail against external requirements. As a result, the retention policy does not fully reflect all applicable obligations.
forms.corrective:
The laboratory shall revise the Control of “Procedure for Control of Management System Documents ETAL-QMS-P-803 “to incorporate a dedicated section addressing the requirements of ISO/IEC 17025:2017 Clause 8.4 (Control of Records). This revision will ensure that all record control elements—including identification, storage, protection, backup, retention, retrieval, access control, archiving, and disposal—are clearly defined and integrated within a single, comprehensive procedure.
The laboratory will revise the Procedure for Control of Management System Documents ETAL-QMS-P-803 to ensure record retention periods are defined based on applicable legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements instead of a fixed duration.

rcas.statement: a) The Lab has developed the Procedure for Technical Record (ETAL-LAB-P-705, Issue No. 01, Rev.No.00) and procedure “Control of Management System Documents (ETAL-QMS-P-803, Issue No. 01, Rev No. 00)” to manage and control the Technical & Quality Records. Lab needs to revise these SOPs or develop another SOP for this clause of standard as these SOPs do not cover all the requirements of this clause of standard.
whys: Because the procedures did not fully address all requirements of ISO/IEC 17025:2017 Clause 8.4 for control of records.
Because key elements (e.g., storage, backup, retention, access, archiving, disposal) were only partially covered, mainly within the technical records procedure.
Because record control requirements were distributed across multiple procedures without proper integration into a single, unified system.
Because the QMS procedures were developed and maintained separately, without a comprehensive approach to align all record control requirements as required by Clause 8.4.
rcas.conclusion: Control of Records Procedure (ETAL-LAB-P-705) and Control of Management System Documents Procedure (ETAL-QMS-P-803) Both procedures are not properly aligned with each other and do not collectively ensure comprehensive coverage of ISO/IEC 17025:2017 Clause 8.4 requirements.

rcas.statement: b) Lab has described the retention period for records is three years: lab needs to rectify its statement about the retention period as the retention period also depends on legal obligations.
whys: Because the laboratory defined a fixed record retention period of three years.
Because it was initially established as a general QMS requirement during system development.
Because external requirements such as legal, regulatory, and contractual obligations were not specifically considered at that stage.
Because the retention policy was developed as a basic standardized approach without a structured review or differentiation of applicable obligations.
rcas.conclusion: ETAL-LAB-P-705 (Technical Records Procedure) and ETAL-QMS-P-803 (Control of Management System Documents) define a fixed three-year retention period as a general QMS requirement without evaluating legal, regulatory, and contractual obligations.

forms.details: The procedure “Reporting of Results” (ETAL-LAB-P-708) lacks specification of the decision rule when not provided by the customer (Clause 7.8.6, ISO/IEC 17025:2017). It also includes “Opinion and Interpretation”, which is not practiced in the laboratory, leading to potential inconsistency and misrepresentation in reporting.
forms.root_cause: The laboratory assumed that customers would always specify the decision rule due to unclear procedural guidance. Additionally, the “Opinion and Interpretation” section was retained from a generic template without reflecting actual laboratory practices. Management identified this as an improvement opportunity to align documentation with ISO/IEC 17025:2017 and current operations.
forms.corrective:
The Reporting of Results procedure (ETAL-LAB-P-708) will be revised to include a defined approach for cases where customers do not specify a decision rule, adopting a default binary acceptance rule with zero guard band. Additionally, Section 6.4 “Opinion and Interpretation” will be removed to accurately reflect the laboratory’s actual practices.
Relevant laboratory personnel will be briefed on the revised procedure and trained on decision rule requirements and their application in test reports.
A communication will be issued to relevant customers outlining the laboratory’s policy on decision rules and the default approach applied when none is specified.
notes: Improvement NC raised by the CEO; no RCA form in the record.

forms.details: It was observed that test reports issued from different ETAL laboratory sites (Karachi and Lahore) were generated with identical report identification numbers (e.g., 202510001) without any site-specific differentiation. This practice does not ensure unique report identification and may lead to ambiguity, traceability issues, and potential misinterpretation of reports.
forms.root_cause: The duplication of report identification numbers occurred because both sites previously used identical manual numbering formats independently. When both sites transitioned to shared reporting software, the lack of a formal change management and numbering review process led to overlapping report numbers without site-specific differentiation.
forms.corrective:
Implement site-specific identification in all new reports (e.g., prefix codes “KHI-” for Karachi and “LHE-” for Lahore) to ensure unique numbering.
Communicate the new numbering requirement to both sites and relevant personnel.
notes: Improvement NC raised by the CEO; no RCA form in the record.

forms.details: Outcomes related to the complaints are communicated to the customer as per lab’s procedure, however, the requirement of clause 7.9.6 regarding outcome approval by the person in question is not addressed.
forms.root_cause: The Complaint Handling Procedure addressed the complaint resolution process; however, no standardized Complaint Resolution Form had been developed to document the review and approval of complaint outcomes. Consequently, the requirement of ISO/IEC 17025:2017 Clause 7.9.6 was not consistently demonstrated.
forms.corrective: A standardized Complaint Resolution Form will be developed and implemented to document the complaint resolution process, including the independent review and approval of complaint outcomes by an authorized person not involved in the laboratory activities related to the complaint, thereby ensuring compliance with ISO/IEC 17025:2017 Clause 7.9.6.
notes: Improvement NC raised by the CEO; no RCA form in the record.

forms.details: The laboratory needs to replace paper-based raw data sheets (ETAL-LAB-704-FF-05) with electronic records to reduce the potential for personnel errors and improve data integrity.
forms.root_cause: Raw data are recorded and processed using paper-based forms, requiring manual transcription into the reporting system. This manual process creates opportunities for transcription and recording errors. Management identified this as an improvement opportunity to align documentation with ISO/IEC 17025:2017 and current operations.
forms.corrective: Implementation of electronic raw data sheets within the reporting software to eliminate manual transcription, improve data integrity, enhance traceability, and reduce the risk of human error.
notes: Improvement NC raised by the CEO; no RCA form in the record.

forms.details: The laboratory needs to replace the paper-based Work Completion Form (ETAL-LAB-704-FF-08), Customer Feedback Form (ETAL-QMS-806-FF-02) and Improvement Analysis Report (ETAL-QMS-806-FF-01) with an electronic form in the reporting software to streamline the continual improvement process and improve efficiency, accessibility, and record management.
forms.root_cause: Manual completion and storage of work completion records increase administrative effort and reduce the efficiency of record retrieval and tracking. The existing paper-based improvement records require manual preparation and storage, reducing efficiency and making tracking and retrieval more difficult. Reliance on manual paper-based customer feedback records results in inefficient handling, limited accessibility, and increased risk of loss, damage, or incomplete records.
forms.corrective:

Implement an electronic Improvement Analysis Report in the reporting software to improve documentation, traceability, monitoring of improvement activities, and record retention.
Implement an electronic Customer Feedback Form within the reporting software to improve record accessibility, traceability, storage, and timely analysis of customer feedback.
